<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <title>Circle</title>
  <style>
    *,
    *::before,
    *::after {
      box-sizing: border-box;
      margin: 0;
      padding: 0;
    }

    :root {
      --bg: #ffffff;
      --fg: #111111;
    }

    @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
      :root {
        --bg: #111111;
        --fg: #f5f5f5;
      }
    }

    html,
    body {
      height: 100%;
    }

    body {
      display: grid;
      place-items: center;
      min-height: 100vh;
      min-height: 100dvh;
      background: var(--bg);
      color: var(--fg);
      overflow: hidden;
    }

    svg {
      display: block;
      width: min(400px, 80vmin);
      height: auto;
      aspect-ratio: 1 / 1;
    }

    .circle {
      fill: currentColor;
    }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <svg id="ae683f770" viewBox="0 0 400 400" role="img" aria-labelledby="circle-title">
    <title id="circle-title">A solid circle</title>
    <circle class="circle" cx="200" cy="200" r="200"/>
  </svg>
</body>
</html>

content.text:
Updated `0.html` with these changes:

- **No stray scrollbar.** Replaced `width: 100vw` with a full-height grid layout, which avoids the horizontal overflow that `100vw` causes when a vertical scrollbar exists. Also uses `100dvh` so mobile browser chrome doesn't clip the page.
- **Responsive SVG.** The circle is now capped at 400px but shrinks to 80% of the smaller viewport dimension on small screens instead of overflowing.
- **Accessibility.** Added `role="img"` and an SVG `<title>` so screen readers announce the graphic, and gave the page a readable title.
- **Themable colour.** The circle fills with `currentColor`, driven by CSS variables that flip for light and dark mode via `prefers-color-scheme`.
- **Box-sizing reset** added to the universal selector for predictable sizing.

The visual result is unchanged in light mode: a centred solid circle. Open the file in a browser to confirm.
